newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 1.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 1.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp. has told Leo Burnett Co. it will have to defend its lead position on the fast-food chain's $600 million advertising account, according to sources. McDonald's told Burnett's it will be competing with DDB Needham Chicago, McDonald's other agency, for the lead portion of the business.

FRANKFURT - Sweets manufacturer Katjes Fassin GmbH & Co awards its advertising account for Dr. Hillers candy to Frankfurt's Agentur Publicis, Publicis says. The agency says it won the seven-figure account against rivals Scholz & Friends, of Berlin, and Boros, of Wuppertal.

PHILADELPHIA - Campbell Soup Co's newly appointed president and chief executive, Dale Morrison, plans to stick with the company's existing strategic plan for boosting sales and earnings growth, which places a strong emphasis on increased advertising he says.

PALM BEACH, Florida - The Hill and Knowlton company, which for decades helped promote smoking, is partially dismissed from Florida's billion-dollar lawsuit against tobacco companies. A judge rules that the public relations firm could not be held liable for health injuries because it was never involved in the manufacture or sale of cigarettes.

INDIANAPOLIS, Indiana - Drug manufacturing giant Eli Lilly and Co. says it will begin consumer advertising for Prozac, its top-selling anti-depressant. It will launch a campaign in August in national consumer magazines, including Newsweek.

AKRON, Ohio - Goodyear Tyre & Rubber Co., America's largest tyremaker, has settled its lawsuit challenging rival Bridgestone/Firestone Inc.'s comparative advertising campaign. The companies would not disclose terms of the settlement.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - WPP Group Plc, the world's largest advertising and marketing group, says its reportable revenues fell slightly in the first five months of 1997 due to the strength of sterling, but world-wide revenues rose seven percent on a constant currency basis.

BUDAPEST - Hungary's National Television and Radio Board says it awards the franchises for Hungary's two new commercial TV channels to Swedish-Hungarian consortium MTM-SBS and a consortium led by CLT, which owns Radio et Television de Luxembourg.

WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration's new "hands off" policy for the Internet has attracted widespread praise, say industry experts. Commerce over the Internet, which includes everything from sales of books and compact disks to fine wines and cheeses, is projected to grow to about $5 billion to $10 billion by the year 2000 from less than $1 billion in 1996, they say.
MUNICH - German public broadcaster ARD acquires re-broadcast rights for the Bundesliga soccer package from from sports rights marketing agency ISPR GmbH for the 1997/98 season.

WILMINGTON, Delaware - Viacom Inc, which owns Paramount Pictures, MTV and Nickelodeon, asks a judge to hold a public auction of USA Networks, the cable partnership it jointly owns with Seagram Co Ltd. According to court documents, Viacom chose the auction remedy after its offer to buy Seagram's half of the partnership for $1.94 billion was rejected.
NEW YORK - Taking its first foray into the long-hyped world of interactive television, General Electric Co's NBC unit says it will offer interactivity in its autumn programme schedule.

SINGAPORE - The Singapore government will not renew the publication licence of IS Magazine following objections to its personal advertisement section, its publisher says. The Ministry of Information and the Arts says the magazine contravened guidelines against exploitation of sex to sell magazines and encouraged undesirable lifestyles.

WASHINGTON - The U.S. government hails a World Trade Organisation ruling against Canadian magazine laws which impose an 80 percent tax on advertising in U.S. magazines that publish editions in Canada, officials say.
LONDON - Britain's Freemasons, a secretive men's organisation, are trying to shake off their image of strange rituals and secret handshakes by launching a "funky" lifestyle magazine this week.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

NEW YORK - Ford Motor Corp and Citicorp say they plan to discontinue their joint venture that gives holders of a Citibank credit card a rebate on every purchase that can be put toward buying a new car, the Wall Street Journal says.
LONDON - Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc says it has sold its John West Foods business to H.J. Heinz Co for an undisclosed sum.
PARIS - French drinks group Pernod Ricard is taking a cautious approach to alliances but remains pragmatic and responsive to the market, its chairman says.

LONDON - British supermarket retailer ASDA Group Plc says it is launching the industry's biggest ever sale of books at half the recommended retail levels or less. ASDA was a major player in a campaign which smashed the UK's Net Book Agreement, which allowed publishers to set retail prices.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch brewer Grolsch says it is not currently in talks about a take-over of its business and had no plans to start such discussions soon. There have been persistent market rumours in Amsterdam in recent days that Grolsch is a likely bid target.
DUESSELDORF - Volkswagen AG is planning to build a small version of its Lup car in China, according to a newspaper report. The car would be smaller than the VW's smallest car, the Polo.
CONSUMER TRENDS

VIENNA - Austria's crucial tourism industry is weathering a difficult summer as locals holiday abroad and foreign visitors by-pass the nation's Alpine charms, the Economy Ministry says. It forecast a summer tourism deficit of around eight billion schillings ($651.2 million), down from a one billion schillings surplus in the summer of 1996.
TOKYO - Japanese working women suffer from sexual harassment and obstacles to equal opportunity at worse levels than women in other industrialised nations, a government report says.

JAKARTA - Southeast Asia's rapidly growing mega-cities are choking in poisonous clouds of vehicle exhaust as increasingly affluent populations invest in cars and motorbikes, but governments are now moving to curb the problem by phasing out leaded gasoline.
